aiPhilosophy: I embrace artificial intelligence tools to enhance my productivity and accelerate learning, always grounding my work in integrity, critical thinking, and ownership. I view AI as a powerful co-pilot, not an autonomous replacement for human judgment.

My core commitment is to the quality and authenticity of the final product. Every line of code, design choice, and written statement is ultimately owned, reviewed, and validated by me. Leveraging AI to misrepresent my capabilities or experiences is fundamentally opposed to my guiding principles.

principles.definition: I build ethically and communicate transparently.
I deliver solutions people can trust.
I am committed to solving hard problems.
I see projects through to impact.
I build what matters, not just what works.
I prioritize clear and respectful communication.

story: My user-focused approach shows up across every product I build. It started with SkySong, an interactive sheet music and audio playback app I designed and built after identifying a real need as a musician, one that reduced chorus members' individual part learning time by 80% after I incorporated feedback from over 20 beta testers. I took full ownership of the entire product lifecycle, maintaining the platform, addressing bugs, and prioritizing enhancement requests based on what users actually needed.

That same instinct drives my work today. As an iOS Developer with Cornell AppDev, I build Uplift in SwiftUI, collaborating with backend and design to ship reliable features. As a Tech Developer Intern with Sponsors for Educational Opportunity, I led frontend development for MatchMission, a nonprofit platform recognized with SEO's Best Integration and Architecture Award, engineering full-stack features people could actually rely on.

Across all of it, I keep coming back to the same commitment: building ethically and anticipating what users actually need. I believe impactful software is born from persistence, empathy, and a creative spark, and that's the thread running through everything here.
